chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hisham ibn Salim, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'What do you say about a man who points a finger at Ali (peace be upon him)?' So he said to me, 'His blood is permissible, by Allah, if it is not permeated by presumed innocence.' I said, 'So what do you say about a man who is hurting us?' He said, 'With regards to what?' I said, 'He is hurting us regarding you, by mentioning you (in derogatory terms)?' So he said to me, 'Is there a share for him with regards to Ali (peace be upon him)?' I said, 'He is saying that and manifesting it.' He said, 'Do not meddle with him.'

key_terms.سَبَّابَةٍ: Pointing a finger (often used for cursing or insulting)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on killing someone who insults Imam Ali (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that insulting Imam Ali (peace be upon him) renders one 'halal al-damm' (worthy of execution), a ruling rooted in the high status of the Imam as the gate to God's knowledge, while cautioning against killing an innocent by mistake. For those who cause annoyance through subtle or implicit references rather than explicit insults, the Imam advises patience and non-confrontation, reflecting the Shia principle of distinguishing between major and minor offenses in political and social contexts. This distinction highlights the pragmatic approach of the Imams in maintaining community stability while preserving the sanctity of the Ahl al-Bayt.
